chunks: the people of the world pass mornings and evenings in different conditions? Thus, (somewhere) the dead is wept for, someone is being condoled, someone is prostrate in distress, someone is enquiring about sick, someone is passing his last breath, some-one is hankering after the world while death is looking for him, someone is forgetful but he is not forgotten (by death), and on the footsteps of the predecessors walk the survivors.
ai.seo_question: What are the different states of people in this world according to Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) uses the vivid imagery of daily life and death to illustrate the *fana* (transience) of the world, a core theme in Shia *zuhd* (asceticism) literature. This passage serves as a spiritual wake-up call, reminding believers that despite their varied pursuits or heedlessness, the inevitable end (*al-baqi*) awaits all, urging them to prepare for the Hereafter while still in the realm of action.
